title: Dispatch CSA 9: Calder Inquiry Names Four Survivors and Three Lost Witnesses
summary: The Institute closes its aperture but preserves the account of the first return.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The Eidetical Institute has issued its final public finding on the Calder Survey. Four members of the party that departed on 30 March survived. The three who appeared in Alderwick before that departure remain missing and are listed in the inquiry as witnesses whose fate cannot be established.

The finding rejects an early proposal to strike the returnees from the record as an instrument error. They occupied rooms, spoke to relatives, left handwritten logs, and built the receiver that guided the later party home. Dr. Marr said their testimony must remain in the archive even if the route by which they reached Alderwick no longer exists.

Mr. Rook, who has resumed his duties, has read the pages left by his other self. He disputes their final conclusion. “He thought Ada had died because he had to leave her,” he said. “I understand why he wrote it. I also understand why he hid it.” He has asked the Institute to retain both accounts beside one another.

Miss Quill visited her father yesterday and returned to the Institute this morning. She has requested that the sealed ranging spindle be studied rather than destroyed. Its brass surface now bears two engraved lines of bearing. One points to the Institute aperture. The other points to the storeroom at East Quay. Neither line was present before the expedition, according to Miss Bell’s plans.

The Calder entrance is closed, and no further opening has been observed. At the inquiry’s close, Dr. Marr read the four survivors’ names aloud. Miss Quill then asked her to read three more: Elian Vey, Silas Rook, and Mara Bell. The clerk entered them beneath the first four, with a space left for the date on which they arrived.
